content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing problems with the battery backup of the real-time clock (RTC). I'm finishing a project involving 20 [product_name] units ([version_no], [article_no]). Initially, none of the devices maintained RTC after power down. After keeping them powered for 24 hours, only three now retain the time correctly. Is anyone aware if these units have a battery or capacitor for RTC backup? It seems unreasonable that a backup battery would need over 24 hours of charging to function. I'm leaving the remaining units powered for another 24 hours before deciding whether to continue troubleshooting.
The [product_name] does not have a backup battery; instead, it uses a SuperCap for RTC backup.
Hi, here's an update. After an additional 24 hours (total of 48 hours powered on), only one more [product_name] started retaining RTC after power down.

Hello, RTC backup failure is a known issue with some new [product_name] units, but there is a solution. I resolved it on all my affected units by performing a factory reset, then verifying if the RTC time was saved after re-powering the device. If successful, the RTC time will be retained after power off. For some of my units, keeping them powered for around 30 minutes after the factory reset helped the backup start working properly.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report that the RTC (Real Time Clock) backup does not reliably function on multiple [product_name] ([version_no], [article_no]) units. Many units failed to retain RTC after power loss, and attempts to resolve by keeping the devices powered produced inconsistent results. Ultimately, performing a factory reset was required to enable proper RTC backup, highlighting issues with reliability and initial user experience.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the RTC backup on all [product_name] units to work dependably right out of the box, without lengthy charging or complex procedures. They also expect clear product documentation explaining RTC backup mechanisms and consistent reliability immediately upon use.
